newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says curbing short-term capital inflows.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says curbing short-term capital inflows.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said it was managing to discourage short term capital inflows and influence the maturity structure of foreign borrowings by banks from the short to longer terms.
"Measures...implemented by the Bank of Thailand (BOT) since August 1995 have started to show positive results," a BOT statement said late on Tuesday.

Capital inflows through non-resident baht accounts declined from the average of 31.80 billion baht per month in the first quarter of 1996 to 3.70 billion per month in the second quarter, the central bank said.

The statement followed Moody's Investors Services's downgrading of Thailand's short-term sovereign ceiling ratings for bank deposits and other short-term obligations to Prime 2 from Prime 1. Short-term rating of the Kingdom of Thailand's commercial paper programme was also affected by the downgrade.
Moody's said the onset of financial liberalisation coupled with a relatively-rigid foreign exchange system had triggered a massive inflow of short-term funding seeking higher yields in Thailand.

"The downgrade reflects the country's increased vulnerability to a financial shock through the balance of payments as a result of the very rapid and recent accumulation of short-term external debt," the rating agency said.

The BOT said recent buildup of Thailand's short-term debt of US$41 billion predominantly reflected the funding of offshore loans by banks operating Bangkok International Banking Facility facilities in Thailand.
"These offshore borrowings are done primarily through intra-office borrowings with their branches or headquarters abroad," it added.
The BOT said offshore borrowings were normally booked as short-term transfers in its balance of payments accounting.
"Therefore it imparts a bias towards short-term debt even though the actual funding of the debt by overseas entities includes longer-term funding," it said.

"If we deduct these intra-bank borrowings, short-term debt amounts to only US$22.8 billion compared to our total gross reserves of US$50.1 billion (US$39.4 billion in official reserves plus 10.7 net assets position of commercial banks)," the central bank added.
